---
title: "flavorizr.lock"
description: "The format of the lock: what flavorizr records, and how."
---

`flavorizr.lock` is the memory of what flutter_flavorizr applied to a project.
It lives in the root of the project and **is meant to be committed**: it lets a
run remove what an earlier run generated (for example a flavor that was dropped
from the configuration) and tell a change made by the tool from one made by
hand.

It is written only after a run fully succeeded, and never edited by hand.

## Example

```yaml
# flavorizr.lock: generated by flutter_flavorizr, do not edit.
# Commit this file: it lets flavorizr remove what it generated.
flavorizrVersion: 3.0.0
flavors:
  dev: sha256:5f2c0a
  prod: sha256:91be44
processors:
  android:buildGradle:
    files:
      android/app/build.gradle:
        hash: sha256:7a1d02
        ownership: patched
  flutter:flavors:
    files:
      lib/flavors.g.dart:
        hash: sha256:c3d9f1
        ownership: managed
      lib/flavors.dart:
        hash: sha256:4be0a2
        ownership: scaffold
  ios:xcodeproj:
    objects:
      ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:
        - 41CBCBB2C9EC2CFF0019D008
        - C93DD37D645EA448590670D3
  ios:plist:
    keys:
      ios/Runner/Info.plist:
        CFBundleDisplayName: sha256:0d44ab
  ios:buildTargets:
    keys:
      ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:
        project/C93DD37D645EA448590670D3/SWIFT_VERSION: sha256:5cc31a
        target/0A5C1A5E4B1C0D2F3E4A5B6C/PRODUCT_NAME: sha256:9d8e1f
  android:icons:
    files:
      android/app/src/dev/res/mipmap-hdpi/ic_launcher.png:
        hash: sha256:73c0de
        ownership: managed
    inputs:
      android/app/src/dev/res/mipmap-hdpi/ic_launcher.png: sha256:e8a6b7
schemaVersion: 2
```

## Schema (version 2)

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion` | integer | Version of the lock format. Bumped when the format changes in a way an older flavorizr cannot read: see [Versions of the format](#versions-of-the-format). |
| `flavorizrVersion` | string | Version of flutter_flavorizr that wrote the lock. |
| `flavors` | map | Flavor name to the hash of its resolved configuration. The names are what the engine reads back as `previousFlavors`. |
| `processors` | map | Processor id (for example `android:buildGradle`) to what it owns. |

Each processor has these optional sections, left out when empty:

| Section | Shape | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | path to `{ownership, hash?}` | Whole files. `ownership` is `scaffold`, `managed` or `patched`. `hash` is the hash of the owned content (the whole file for `managed`, the owned parts for `patched`) and is always present for those two. For a `scaffold` it is the hash of what flavorizr wrote, and is present only when flavorizr wrote it (or found it as it would have): see [Scaffold hashes](#scaffold-hashes). |
| `regions` | path to region id to hash | Marked regions of a shared file. |
| `keys` | path to key to hash | Owned keys of a plist, manifest, XML or project file: the hash of the value flavorizr wrote. See [Owned build settings](#owned-build-settings). |
| `objects` | path to list of UUIDs | UUIDs of the pbxproj objects flavorizr created, sorted. See [Owned objects](#owned-objects). |
| `inputs` | output path to hash | Generated binaries such as icons: the hash of the *inputs* (source file hash plus options), never of the output, so bumping a library such as `image` creates no noise. A path is here only when it is also one of the `files`. See [Inputs of generated files](#inputs-of-generated-files). |

Notes:

* Artifacts of the `local` ownership class are **never** stored: they are
  regenerated silently on every run and are neither drift nor conflict.
* Hashes are opaque strings. The engine decides how they are computed (the
  recommended spelling is `<algorithm>:<hex digest>`, such as `sha256:...`).
* Paths are relative to the project root and use `/`.
* `flavors` and `processors` are required on read, the sections of a processor
  are optional. Unknown keys at the same `schemaVersion` are ignored on read.
* A UTF-8 byte order mark at the start of the file is tolerated on read.
* **`project.pbxproj`.** The Xcode project of a platform is shared by every
  Darwin processor (`xcodeproj:ios`, `xcodeproj:macos`) and is a `patched`
  file. The lock records the UUIDs of the objects flavorizr created in it (see
  [Owned objects](#owned-objects)), which is enough to find and remove them, but
  not to *hash* what flavorizr owns: a reader of the owned content gets the file
  alone, and the file does not say which of its objects are flavorizr's. So the
  `ownedContent` reader of the project file says it by what the processors
  write. For now that is what `ios:xcconfig`
  and `macos:configs` own: the file references to the flavor xcconfigs
  (`Flutter/<flavor>Debug.xcconfig` and `Runner/Configs/...`, and the `Profile`
  and `Release` ones, for any flavor) and their entries in a Resources phase,
  which a run removes, and the references that `ios:launchScreen` makes to the
  storyboards of the launch screens (`Runner/<flavor>LaunchScreen.storyboard`).
  An edit of the rest, by Xcode, CocoaPods or Flutter, is not drift. `ios:buildTargets` and `macos:buildTargets` add the
  build settings of the flavors to it (see [Owned build settings](#owned-build-settings)),
  and `ios:firebase` and `macos:firebase` their build phase. **Known limitation:**
  an object another processor owns and does not extend the reader for is recorded
  in `objects` but not hashed, so an edit of it by hand is not seen as drift. A
  test checks that every object `ios:xcconfig` records is one of the lines the
  reader hashes.

## Versions of the format

| `schemaVersion` | What it adds |
| --- | --- |
| `1` | The format of the 3.0 development builds. |
| `2` | The `hash` of a `scaffold` file, and `inputs` filled in for the generated images. |

A lock of version 1 is read as it is: its scaffolds have no hash and no file has
inputs, which means "not known yet", never an error. The next run that writes
the lock writes version 2, with what that run could learn (see below), and no
conflict or change to the project comes from the upgrade itself. A flavorizr
that only knows version 1 refuses a lock of version 2 with a hint to upgrade,
since it would drop what it does not know when it writes the lock again.

## Inputs of generated files

An icon is rendered from an image, and the bytes the renderer makes depend on
the version of the library that encodes them, and on the machine. So that a run
does not rewrite every icon after an update of `package:image`, or on a
colleague's machine, the lock records for each generated image the hash of what
it was made **from**, next to the hash of the file:

```yaml
windows:icons:
  files:
    windows/runner/resources/dev.ico:
      hash: sha256:73c0de
      ownership: managed
  inputs:
    windows/runner/resources/dev.ico: sha256:e8a6b7
```

The hash of the inputs is made of the digest of the bytes of the source image, the
kind of file (`png` or `ico`) and the sizes of its frames, and the label, colour
and area of the badge, if any, plus the version of flavorizr's rendering (it is
bumped when the pixels flavorizr draws change on purpose). The path of the
source, the flavor and the machine are not part of it.

A run asks, for each image: *are the inputs the ones the lock recorded, and is the
file the one the lock recorded?* If both are true the image is neither rendered
nor written, and the plan has nothing to say about it, whatever the renderer would
make today. Otherwise it is rendered as ever:

| What changed | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing | Nothing is rendered or written. |
| The source image (its content), the badge (label, colour, on or off) or the size set | The image is rendered again. |
| Only the path of the source, or the library that encodes the PNG | Nothing. |
| The file was edited by hand | It is rendered again, and a file that differs from what the lock recorded is a conflict, as for any managed file. |
| The file is missing | It is rendered again. |
| The lock has no inputs for it (version 1) | It is rendered again, which is how the lock learns them. |
| The source image is missing or is not an image | The run fails, and nothing is written. |

`flavorizr adopt` (and the adoption of a first run) records the inputs of an image
only when the file on disk is exactly what flavorizr would make from them now: it
cannot tell what a file that is different was made from (2.x had its own
renderer, or the user replaced it), so the next run makes it and says so.

## Scaffold hashes

A `scaffold` file is the user's once it exists, and a run never touches it, so
whatever the user does to it is never drift. The lock still records the hash of
what flavorizr **wrote**, so that a scaffold that flavorizr no longer produces is
dealt with safely:

* a scaffold that is still as it was written is removed silently;
* one that was edited, or whose hash the lock does not have, goes through the
  conflict flow, and nothing is deleted without the user's say.

The hash is recorded when a run creates the file or replaces it with
`--overwrite-scaffold`, and also when the file that is there is exactly what the
run would write (which is how a lock of version 1 learns it). A scaffold the user
had before flavorizr, or one the user changed, keeps whatever the lock had for it:
no hash for the first, the hash of what was written for the second.

## Owned objects

The objects a Darwin processor creates in `project.pbxproj` (the build
configurations of a flavor, the file references of its xcconfig files, a build
phase) are recorded in `objects`, by UUID, so that a later run can remove the
ones that are no longer wanted: a flavor that was dropped, a phase that is not
needed anymore.

Their UUIDs are **deterministic**. Each object gets the first 24 hex characters
of the MD5 of a seed that says what it is:

```text
flavorizr/<platform>/<target>/<flavor>/<kind>[/<detail>...]
```

| Segment | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<platform>` | `ios` or `macos`. |
| `<target>` | The name of the target the object belongs to (`Runner`), or `@project` for an object of the project itself. |
| `<flavor>` | The name of the flavor, or `@all` for an object that does not belong to a flavor. |
| `<kind>`, `<detail>` | What the object is, such as `buildConfiguration/Debug`. |

So `flavorizr/ios/@project/dev/buildConfiguration/Debug` is always
`C93DD37D645EA448590670D3`: two runs from scratch write the same
`project.pbxproj`, and the diff of a run is only what changed. A segment holds
no `/`, and `@` is reserved to the two markers.

What the lock does with them:

* **Only what flavorizr created is recorded.** An object that existed (from
  Flutter, from the user, from 2.x) is used as it is, keeps its UUID, is not
  recorded, and so is never removed, unless the processor knows it is
  flavorizr's (say, a configuration 2.x created) and claims it: the lock then
  records the UUID it has. That is what the [adoption](/reference/adopt#the-xcode-projects)
  of a project 2.x flavorized does, whether `flavorizr adopt` or the first run without a lock. UUIDs are never rewritten for the project
  as a whole: that would break what refers to them from outside the file, such
  as the `BlueprintIdentifier` of a scheme.
* **A processor says what it owns on every run**, and what the lock records for
  it is exactly that: an object it does not own anymore leaves the list, after
  being removed from the project. A processor that tracked the project file and
  said nothing about its objects keeps what the lock had, so that nothing it
  owns is ever forgotten; one that owns none says so with an empty set. A file
  the processor stops tracking takes its objects with it.
* **The record of a file that a run did not write is kept**, with the objects
  it had: when the user chose to keep their version of `project.pbxproj` in a
  conflict, what the run created in memory is not in the file.
* **An object is owned, not its seed.** Flavors that share a file share the
  object that stands for it: the first makes it, the others find it. It stays
  as long as any flavor of the run still needs it, whichever one made it (a
  flavor can be dropped or renamed without taking away what another needs), and
  goes with the last. An object that was recorded for a processor and that the
  run finds again is still owned by it, even when its seed is not the UUID it
  has. What another processor recorded is foreign to this one.
* **Removal is by UUID, cascading.** Each object is removed with
  `removeFromProject`, which also takes the references to it (its entry in a
  configuration list or a build phase, the build files of a file reference), so
  nothing is left dangling. An object the lock lists that is not in the project
  anymore is just forgotten; the project object, its main group and its targets
  are never removed, whatever the lock says, as the lock is a file that can be
  edited or merged.
* **The UUID is the identity.** If the lock is lost, the next run finds the
  objects again by their UUID and records them again, with no change to the
  project.

The format does not change: `objects` is part of schema version 1 and stays
optional, so `schemaVersion` is not bumped, and a lock without it reads as
"nothing created yet".

In code, `PbxprojSeed` and `OwnedObjects` (`lib/src/engine/darwin/`) are what a
processor uses on top of the `xcodeproj:ios` / `xcodeproj:macos` resources:
`ensure` creates or finds an object, `settle` removes the stale ones and tells
the context what the processor owns.

## Owned build settings

`ios:buildTargets` and `macos:buildTargets` edit the build settings of a
configuration **key by key**. 2.x replaced the `buildSettings` of the
configuration on every run, which wiped the `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` chosen in Xcode
(#340). Now flavorizr owns the keys it sets and nothing else, and records them
in `keys`, under `project.pbxproj`:

```yaml
ios:buildTargets:
  keys:
    ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:
      project/C93DD37D645EA448590670D3/SWIFT_VERSION: sha256:5cc31a
      target/0A5C1A5E4B1C0D2F3E4A5B6C/PRODUCT_NAME: sha256:9d8e1f
```

A key is `<scope>/<configuration UUID>/<setting>`: `project` is a configuration
of the project (the settings of the yaml: `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER`,
`SWIFT_VERSION`, and so on), `target` one of the first native target of the
project (`PRODUCT_NAME`). The configuration is told by its UUID, since every
target has a `Debug-dev`. The value is the hash of what flavorizr wrote, as JSON,
in the form the project stores it (a flag string such as `-ObjC -all_load` is a
list in `OTHER_LDFLAGS`).

* **Other settings are never touched.** A `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM`, a
  `CODE_SIGN_STYLE` or anything else you or Xcode put in a configuration
  survives every run.
* **A setting that is not wanted anymore** (it left the yaml, or its flavor did)
  is removed **only when its value is still the one flavorizr wrote**. If you
  changed it, the value is yours: it stays, and flavorizr stops owning it.
* **A configuration that holds settings of yours stays.** The configurations of
  a flavor you remove go with it, unless they hold a setting flavorizr did not
  write (a `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` in the target one, anything that differs from the
  `Debug`, `Profile` or `Release` configuration it started as in the project
  one): they stay in the project, flavorizr stops owning them, and the lock
  forgets them.
* **Editing an owned setting by hand is a conflict.** A run that has to write
  over a value it recorded finds it was changed and asks first, whichever
  processors ran before it: that does not depend on the hash of the file, which
  the other processors that write `project.pbxproj` move. The lock also hashes the
  settings of the `<Mode>-<flavor>` configurations of the project and the
  `PRODUCT_NAME` of the ones of the target (the rest of the target is never
  hashed), so a run that has to write over the value you put asks first, as it
  does for any file you edited.

  The hash covers **every** setting of a project configuration named like a
  flavor one, since the lock cannot tell which of them flavorizr wrote from the
  file alone. A setting you add to one of them by hand does not change what the
  run writes, but it makes the run ask when it also has to change the other
  settings of the flavors; what it writes keeps your setting.

## Determinism

The same logical content is always written to the same bytes, so two runs with
no changes produce a byte-identical lock and merge conflicts stay small. The
lock records `flavorizrVersion`, so the bytes are identical for the same
flutter_flavorizr version: upgrading the tool rewrites that one line.

* every mapping is written with its keys sorted by code unit, and the lists of
  `objects` are sorted;
* two spaces of indentation, `\n` line endings, UTF-8 without BOM, a single
  trailing newline, the same header comment;
* empty sections are left out, and an empty top-level section is written as
  `{}`;
* scalars are plain when that is safe and double quoted otherwise, so a value
  such as `yes`, `1e3` or `a: b` stays a string;
* nothing depends on the time, the machine or the order the content was
  collected in.

The lock is written to a temporary file next to it and then renamed, so an
interrupted write never leaves a truncated lock.

## Version guard

When it reads the lock, flutter_flavorizr checks, before anything else:

* a `schemaVersion` **higher** than the one it writes: the run is blocked, since
  the format is unknown, with a hint to upgrade flutter_flavorizr;
* a `flavorizrVersion` **higher** than the running one (semantic version
  precedence, build metadata ignored): the run is blocked with the same hint,
  since the newer version may have recorded things this one would drop;
* anything older or equal is read normally. A lock of version 1 is read and
  written back as version 2 (see [Versions of the format](#versions-of-the-format));
  when the format changes, the new reader is responsible for the older versions.

A lock that is not valid YAML or does not have the shape above is reported as
malformed, with the file to restore from version control or delete.

## In code

* `FlavorizrLock`, `ProcessorLock` and `LockedFile` (`lib/src/engine/lock/`)
  are the plain data model. `LockedFile` refuses a `local` file and enforces
  the hash rule above.
* `LockCodec.encode` / `LockCodec.decode` convert to and from text, in memory.
* `LockStore` reads and writes the file in the project root.
